about.title: Understory
about.body:
My work is an act of attention. With acrylic and mixed media, I recreate Pacific Northwest ecology through the lens of sensory experience and emotion: moments hiking and exploring when I stop analyzing and simply perceive. I am interested in an intimate way of knowing rooted in the felt experience of being among other living things.

I am drawn to life that dwells and interacts gracefully but is easily overlooked because of its scale or speed: the small, the slow, the very tall, the hard to find. Slugs, insects, dew drops, mosses, lichens, and fungi share my attention with the towering conifers and snags that define the region's landscape. I cherish the interplay of decay and growth. A nurse log is both an ending and a beginning, a body of one tree becoming the ground for many others. These cycles of regeneration remind me that nothing is static or separate.

To translate this heightened awareness to the canvas, I use saturated color, softened focus, and expressive brushwork. Purples glow in the shadows, greens turn electric, and edges dissolve, much as the world does when I am fully absorbed.

Sometimes intensified perception tips into the imagined. In these works, mushrooms may rise from a pond that does not exist, their roots reaching through the water like tentacles. Or spirit-like creatures appear against a burning sunset. Fantastical, sometimes macabre elements are not a departure from observing the landscape but another way of feeling my way into it. Beneath the surface of any forest is a network of hidden, strange, and unseen activity, and to give it form is to acknowledge that the living world is always more than what we see at a glance.

My paintings also pay homage to the ephemeral. Light falls a certain way for only a moment, mist and dew arrive and vanish, and every organism exists in a passing stage of growth or decline. In giving my full attention to these fleeting conditions, I recognize my own impermanence as another creature seeing, sensing, and treasuring this world. My hope is that viewers feel invited to slow down, to look closely at what they might otherwise pass by, and to experience their own sense of connection.

research.title: Research

image.alt: Rowenn Kalman in a sun hat, standing in front of an Andean mural of a woman in a hat and a snow-capped mountain.

research.introEn:
Hello, my name is Rowenn Kalman, PhD. Some people call me Rosita.

I carried out an anthropological study of environmental awareness in Áncash, Peru. This is my thesis, with a summary in Spanish. A preliminary report I wrote in Spanish in 2011 is also available.
research.introEs:
Hola, mi nombre es Rowenn Kalman, PhD. Algunos me llaman Rosita.

Hice un estudio antropológico sobre la conciencia ambiental en Áncash, Perú. Esta es mi tesis, con un resumen en español. También está disponible un informe preliminar que hice en español el año 2011.
